name: Circular design & disassembly documentation
missing_elements_and_limitations: ISO 20887 sets DfD/A principles but defines no machine-readable data fields, handover templates, or minimum data sets for digital platforms. No link to IFC property sets or DPP schemas. Guidance only; no normative performance levels.

name: Circular design & disassembly documentation
missing_elements_and_limitations: Provides generic data-template framework and taxonomy model. Explicitly states it does not provide content of any templates. No reuse-specific domain template for condition grades, disassembly sequences, or circular potential. REINCARNATE CP-IM JSON schemas reveal concrete missing fields.

name: Circular design & disassembly documentation
missing_elements_and_limitations: Provides a B2B methodology for circularity data exchange. Does not specify construction-component-specific fields (connection types, disassembly sequence, embodied-carbon history, reuse pathway). DPP/ESPR alignment for construction components not yet defined.

name: Circular design & disassembly documentation
missing_elements_and_limitations: LoIN defines methodology for specifying information requirements in BIM. Does not define reuse-oriented LoIN profiles for dismantled components. A reuse-LoIN specification is absent.
type_of_gap: Missing application/profile — LoIN methodology exists in new standard; reuse-domain profile still absent

name: Circular design & disassembly documentation
missing_elements_and_limitations: Provides semantic modelling patterns including material chemistry and measurement support. Does not include circularity-specific or reuse-specific modelling patterns. REINCARNATE Ontology (ReOn) lacks a normative anchor.

name: Circular design & disassembly documentation
missing_elements_and_limitations: Provides 6-step refurbishment assessment methodology (incl. Step 2: Sustainable deconstruction). References EN 15978, EN 16309, EN 16627 but does not define reuse-pathway criteria, component salvage scoring, or material-harvest triggers. No integration with CP-IM or digital twin representation. No normative circularity performance levels.

name: Circularity metrics & data structures
missing_elements_and_limitations: Specifies a multi-level framework for measuring circularity. Does not define construction-sector-specific KPIs, component-level indicators, or a mapping to BIM objects or CP-IM data fields. No bridge to EN 15978 LCA.

name: Circularity metrics & data structures
missing_elements_and_limitations: EN 15978 covers whole-building LCA but does not address component-level reuse scenarios or standardised attribution of embodied-carbon savings to reclaimed parts. REINCARNATE innovations (RAS, BAM, TUB) generate CO?-savings data with no standard reporting format.

name: Circularity metrics & data structures
missing_elements_and_limitations: Provides framework for environmental, social and economic performance of buildings. Does not address secondary/reclaimed component streams or circular interventions. Background reference only.

name: Circularity metrics & data structures
missing_elements_and_limitations: Provides a framework for sustainability of civil engineering works. No circularity-specific indicators or reuse data structures. Relevant to VIAS demo site (infrastructure).

name: Circularity metrics & data structures
missing_elements_and_limitations: Directly targets CE in construction. Specifies framework, principles, definitions and alignment for product TCs. Does not yet exist as a published standard. REINCARNATE demo evidence could directly inform this work item.
type_of_gap: Missing standard — now registered as prEN 18177

name: Circularity metrics & data structures
missing_elements_and_limitations: Directly relevant: this work item will produce gap analysis conclusions and recommendations for CEN/TC 350/SC1. REINCARNATE's T5.4/D5.5 is precisely the evidence this work item is designed to absorb. Highest direct contribution opportunity in the project.
type_of_gap: Work item cancelled — gap analysis function absorbed or abandoned

name: Material traceability & reuse workflows
missing_elements_and_limitations: Does not define construction-specific component identifiers, provenance chains, or handover protocols for components crossing organisational boundaries. REINCARNATE CP-IM uses JSON+REST; no normative counterpart exists.

name: Material traceability & reuse workflows
missing_elements_and_limitations: No current ISO or CEN standard defines machine-readable traceability data for CDW fractions (concrete, brick, timber, glass) compatible with digital delivery tickets and CP-IM JSON. EN 50625 / ISO 15270 cover material codes only — full traceability chain is unstandardised.

name: Material traceability & reuse workflows
missing_elements_and_limitations: IDM provides methodology for linking business processes to information delivery in BIM. No reuse-specific delivery specification exists. D5.3's gate-based process model is effectively a proto-IDM for reuse that should be developed into a normative specification.

name: Material traceability & reuse workflows
missing_elements_and_limitations: No standard addresses ownership, liability, warranty, or guarantee framework for secondary/reclaimed construction materials crossing organisational boundaries.

name: Material traceability & reuse workflows
missing_elements_and_limitations: ISO/AWI 59014 is an Active Work Item that will directly address secondary materials traceability — the core of REINCARNATE GAP 3.2 and GAP 3.4. At AWI stage, no content yet available. Critical opportunity: REINCARNATE evidence (CDW flows, CP-IM provenance fields, demo site data) can directly inform this standard. No construction-specific scope confirmed yet — there is a risk this becomes generic/non-construction-focused without sector input.
type_of_gap: No relevant content yet (AWI stage) — new standard

name: BIM fragmentation & interoperability
missing_elements_and_limitations: IFC is the backbone for BIM exchange across REINCARNATE. Revision extends infrastructure coverage but lacks standardised property sets for reuse classification, disassembly sequences, and circular potential. Extensions are project-specific and not normalised.

name: BIM fragmentation & interoperability
missing_elements_and_limitations: ISO 19650 is the reference standard for CDE and information management. No part addresses reuse-specific workflows, component lifecycle tracking across ownership changes, or circular handover protocols. Certification cost is a cited barrier.
type_of_gap: Standard scope insufficient — reuse workflow absent

name: BIM fragmentation & interoperability
missing_elements_and_limitations: Will detail CDE as collaborative BIM workflow, including linking to Asset Management Systems and Open API for CDE (TC442 WG2). Does not address reuse-specific data storage or secondary material API profiles. CP-IM architecture extends beyond this TR.
type_of_gap: Published TR — scope confirmed; reuse-specific API profiles still absent

name: BIM fragmentation & interoperability
missing_elements_and_limitations: Provides recommendations for BIM object library format and content. Does not define representation of reclaimed or upgraded components, or reuse-relevant properties (condition, origin, residual life). 3L's URRBC ontology is a reuse library extension with no normative standard to align to.

name: BIM fragmentation & interoperability
missing_elements_and_limitations: No current standard defines open API profiles or JSON data-exchange formats for circular component information management platforms (CP-IM equivalents). D5.3 Section 7.4 proposes submitting JSON templates and OpenAPI bundles to buildingSMART and CEN/TC 442.

name: BIM fragmentation & interoperability
missing_elements_and_limitations: Confirmed scope: manufacturer-to-designer data exchange for MEP building services equipment only. Not applicable to structural/envelope components (concrete, timber, brick, glass). Relevant only as a structural reference for how product catalogues could be extended.

name: Circularity in procurement & value chains
missing_elements_and_limitations: Provides guidance for organisations transitioning from linear to circular business models. Contains no operational templates for circular procurement criteria, reuse component tendering, or supply-chain validation.

name: Circularity in procurement & value chains
missing_elements_and_limitations: EPD standard does not address EPDs for secondary or reclaimed materials, nor specify how recycled content and circular value flows are disclosed. BAM's SLAMD CO?-savings results have no standard EPD format.

name: Circularity in procurement & value chains
missing_elements_and_limitations: Links EPD data to BIM workflows. Applicable only to virgin products with existing EPDs. No template or mechanism for reclaimed component sustainability declarations within BIM. REINCARNATE CO?-savings data lacks a standard BIM property set.

name: Circularity in procurement & value chains
missing_elements_and_limitations: Establishes sustainability indicators for civil engineering works. Does not address circularity-specific indicators or reuse performance. Relevant to VIAS demo site.

name: Circularity in procurement & value chains
missing_elements_and_limitations: Reviews characteristics of CE value networks. Not normative. Relevant as background for REINCARNATE's D5.2 value chain analysis. REINCARNATE data could enrich this TR.

name: Product re-certification & re-approval
missing_elements_and_limitations: No standard defines a re-certification or re-approval schema for construction products and components after removal from a building. In Germany (and likely Europe-wide), product approval (Zulassung) lapses at installation AND at removal. No standardised process for Second Life assessment of building components exists.

name: Ownership & liability of secondary materials
missing_elements_and_limitations: No standard addresses ownership transfer, liability, warranty, or guarantee frameworks for secondary/reclaimed construction materials or components crossing organisational boundaries. Directly impedes market-scale reuse: actors cannot define contractual responsibilities without a normative reference. CP-IM records ownership and component history but has no normative liability framework to reference.

name: National & sectoral: deconstruction and CDW
missing_elements_and_limitations: ÖNORM B 3151 (ASI) specifies selective deconstruction, mono-material separation, and hazardous substance identification — directly relevant to REINCARNATE's pre-demolition inventory and CDW traceability goals. DIN 18007:2022 provides German equivalent. Neither is a European standard; no CEN counterpart exists. Gap: no EN-level standard for selective deconstruction method with reuse-optimised separation requirements. REINCARNATE results (robotic deconstruction, HUST material codes, demo-site protocols) could support NWIP for EN-level standard.

name: National & sectoral: deconstruction and CDW
missing_elements_and_limitations: EN 206 and EN 12620 include recycled aggregate provisions but with density limits and quality caveats. Expert 4 (VIAS) notes 'always have a limit'; continuous updating needed. prEN 197-6 (cement with recycled materials) under approval — new CEN standard. Gap: no comprehensive high-quality recycled aggregate certification pathway that integrates with REINCARNATE CP-IM provenance data.
type_of_gap: Standard scope insufficient for high-quality reuse pathway
